items.title: Clem Raymond Interview, 1958-08-25
items.q: They all died out there, folks. Yeah, both of the Spike brothers dead. Slocum's dead.

ctx.x: Yeah, his brother-in-law. Mm-hmm. And Dick, one piece he played, sort of the slow blues. And I said, what's the name of that? He said, well, call it the So Different Blues. And I thought that was a funny name, but I never know it came from the band. I wondered where he got that. He never didn't mean much to me.

Well, I was out there in 1919. Who? I said, well, I was out there in 1919. Yeah. They called it Band of So Different Band. Mm-hmm. They all died out there, folks. Yeah, both of the Spike brothers dead. Slocum's dead. Cheryl Green, he's dead? Yeah. And Doc was the drummer. He got killed in the tube over there, Stockton Tunnel, rather. They all was dead, and Sid's the only one left. And he's about to pass. How's that fight? How's that? Harris Sutherland, he's living? Who? Harris Sutherland. Oh, no, Harris wasn't…
You know, we tried to find out where Wade Whaley was. And nobody down there knew Paul Howard thought he was up this way. Maybe he said try San Jose.
